A free d4 on an ally's ability check. Use it constantly outside combat.
Booming voice and small omens; surprisingly persuasive.
The straightforward heal when someone needs real hit points back.
A bonus action revive at range. Often better than Cure Wounds in a fight.

A light source and a ranged attack in one.
Lets you fight with your club using Wisdom, so you need no Strength.

Ten berries that each heal 1 hit point and feed someone for a day. Quietly one of the best 1st-level spells.
Restrains a group of enemies in a 20-foot square.

A d4 on attacks and saves for three allies. Almost always your best use of a slot.
Healing on top of Lay on Hands.
A bonus action for +2 AC on you or an ally.
Pins one dangerous enemy on you and away from the squishy party members.
An extra 1d6 on every hit against your target, all day. Take this first.
Cheap healing and food that solves survival problems.

Handles things you would rather not touch yourself.

Your big single-target hit, in whatever damage type the fight needs.
The best attack cantrip in the game and the core of most warlocks. Take it.
Extra damage on every hit plus disadvantage on one ability. Pairs perfectly with Eldritch Blast.
Temporary hit points that hurt anyone who hits you, and it scales beautifully with your slots.
A reaction that punishes whoever just damaged you.

A free d4 on ability checks, all day.
Repairs objects, which comes up more than you would think.
You are often the party's only healer.

Ranged damage for when you cannot reach the fight.
Hits harder against armored foes and stops opportunity attacks as you step away.
No torch to hold, so your shield hand stays free.

Damage that always lands, for the flier you cannot reach.
Pushes a crowd off you and hurts every one of them.
Shuts down charm, fear and possession from the creatures that use them.

Turns a hostile guard into a friendly one for an hour.

Makes you or a friend hard to attack while you slip away.

Light in your hand, and ranged fire damage when you need it.
Ten more feet of speed for an hour: in and out before anyone reacts.

Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. Standing up from prone costs only 5 feet of movement, climbing costs no extra movement, and you can make a running jump after moving only 5 feet.

Increase your Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20. You have advantage on Deception and Performance checks when passing yourself off as someone else, and you can mimic the speech or sounds of a creature you have heard for at least 1 minute.

After you Dash, you can use a bonus action to make one melee attack or to shove a creature. If you moved at least 10 feet in a straight line first, the attack deals an extra 5 damage or the shove pushes 10 extra feet.

You ignore the loading property of crossbows you are proficient with, being within 5 feet of a hostile creature gives you no disadvantage on ranged attacks, and when you take the Attack action with a one-handed weapon you can use a bonus action to attack with a hand crossbow you are holding.

When a creature hits you with a melee attack while you wield a finesse weapon you are proficient with, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack, possibly turning it into a miss.
You gain +1 AC while wielding a separate melee weapon in each hand, you can two-weapon fight with weapons that lack the light property, and you can draw or stow two one-handed weapons at once.

You have advantage on Perception and Investigation checks to detect secret doors, advantage on saving throws against traps, resistance to trap damage, and you can search for traps while travelling at a normal pace.
Increase your Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20. When you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, the minimum you regain is twice your Constitution modifier.

Increase your Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20. Whenever you have advantage on an attack roll using Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can reroll one of the dice once. The server rolls a third d20 and keeps the highest.

Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder. Your spells of that damage type ignore resistance, and any 1 rolled on their damage dice counts as a 2. You can take this feat more than once, choosing a different type each time.

On a critical hit or when you drop a creature to 0 hit points with a melee weapon, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action. Before attacking with a heavy weapon you are proficient with, you can take a -5 penalty to the attack roll in exchange for +10 damage on a hit.

When you stabilize a creature with a healer's kit it also regains 1 hit point. As an action you can spend a use of a healer's kit to restore 1d6 + 4 hit points plus the creature's Hit Dice to a creature, once each per rest.
Increase your Strength by 1, to a maximum of 20, and gain proficiency with heavy armor.
Increase your Strength by 1, to a maximum of 20. While you wear heavy armor, bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks is reduced by 3.

You can spend 10 minutes rallying up to six friendly creatures within 30 feet who can hear and understand you. Each gains temporary hit points equal to your level plus your Charisma modifier, and cannot benefit again until it finishes a rest.

Increase your Intelligence by 1, to a maximum of 20. You always know which way is north and how many hours remain before sunrise or sunset, and you accurately recall anything you have seen or heard in the past month.
Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20, and gain proficiency with light armor.

Increase your Intelligence by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn three languages and can create written ciphers that others cannot read without an Intelligence check against a DC of 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and proficiency bonus.

You have three luck points, regained on a long rest. Spend one to roll an extra d20 on your own attack roll, ability check or saving throw and choose which die to use, or to roll an extra d20 on an attack made against you and choose which the attacker uses.

Choose a class: bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock or wizard. You learn two cantrips of your choice from that class's spell list. Choose one 1st-level spell from the same list: you learn it and can cast it once without expending a spell slot, at its lowest level, and again after a long rest. Your spellcasting ability for these spells depends on the class you chose: Charisma for bard, sorcerer or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; Intelligence for wizard.

When a creature within 5 feet casts a spell you can use your reaction to attack it. When you damage a creature concentrating on a spell it has disadvantage on the concentration save, and you have advantage on saves against spells cast by creatures within 5 feet.
You learn two maneuvers from the Battle Master list and gain one superiority die of d6, which refills on a short or long rest.
Wearing medium armor does not impose disadvantage on Stealth checks, and if your Dexterity is 16 or higher you add 3 rather than 2 to your AC from medium armor.

Your speed increases by 10 feet, difficult terrain costs no extra movement when you Dash, and when you make a melee attack against a creature it cannot make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of the turn.
Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20, and gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.

While mounted you have advantage on melee attacks against unmounted creatures smaller than your mount, you can redirect an attack aimed at your mount to yourself, and your mount takes no damage on a successful Dexterity save and half on a failure.
Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20. You can read lips, and you gain a +5 bonus to your passive Perception and passive Investigation.

When you take the Attack action with a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff or spear you can use a bonus action to strike with the opposite end for 1d4 bludgeoning damage. You also get an opportunity attack when a creature enters your reach with such a weapon.
Increase one ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20, and gain proficiency in saving throws with that ability.
You gain a ritual book holding two 1st-level ritual spells from a class you choose, and you can cast any ritual in it. You can add further rituals of a level you can cast to the book by copying them.

A creature you hit with an opportunity attack has its speed reduced to 0 for that turn, creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they Disengage, and when a creature within 5 feet attacks someone other than you, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against it.

Attacking at long range gives you no disadvantage, your ranged attacks ignore half and three-quarters cover, and before a ranged attack with a weapon you are proficient with you can take a -5 penalty to the attack roll in exchange for +10 damage on a hit.

If you take the Attack action you can use a bonus action to shove a creature within 5 feet with your shield. You add your shield's AC bonus to Dexterity saves against effects that target only you, and you can use a reaction to take no damage on a successful Dexterity save.
You can hide when lightly obscured, missing with a ranged attack does not reveal your position, and dim light does not impose disadvantage on your Perception checks that rely on sight.
The range of your attack-roll spells doubles, they ignore half and three-quarters cover, and you learn one attack cantrip from the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock or wizard list.

Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20. You are proficient with improvised weapons, your unarmed strike deals 1d4 damage, and when you hit with an unarmed strike or improvised weapon you can use a bonus action to try to grapple.
Your hit point maximum increases by twice your level, and by 2 more each time you gain a level.

You have advantage on Constitution saves to maintain concentration, you can cast with somatic components while holding weapons or a shield, and you can cast a one-action spell targeting one creature as an opportunity attack.
Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20, and gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice.

Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn misty step and one 1st-level divination or enchantment spell, each castable once per long rest without a slot as well as with slots.

Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn invisibility and one 1st-level illusion or necromancy spell, each castable once per long rest without a slot as well as with slots.

Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn mage hand and can cast it without components at 30 extra feet, and as a bonus action you can shove a creature within 30 feet 5 feet on a failed Strength save.

Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20. You can speak telepathically to any creature within 60 feet that shares a language with you, and you can cast detect thoughts once per long rest without a slot.
You learn one Eldritch Invocation of your choice whose prerequisites you meet. You can replace it when you gain a level.
You learn two Metamagic options from the sorcerer list and gain 2 sorcery points to spend on them, refilled on a long rest.
Increase one ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency in one skill, and expertise in one skill you are already proficient in.

Increase your Constitution or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20, and gain proficiency with cook's utensils. Cooking during a short rest lets allies regain an extra 1d8 hit points, and an hour's work makes treats that grant temporary hit points.

Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn when you deal bludgeoning damage you can move the creature 5 feet, and a critical hit with bludgeoning damage gives attackers advantage against it until your next turn.

Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn when you deal piercing damage you can reroll one damage die, and a critical hit with piercing damage adds one extra damage die.

Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn when you deal slashing damage you can reduce the target's speed by 10 feet, and a critical hit with slashing damage gives it disadvantage on attack rolls until your next turn.

You ignore resistance to poison damage, you can coat a weapon as a bonus action so its next hit forces a DC 14 Constitution save for 2d8 poison damage and the poisoned condition, and you gain proficiency with the poisoner's kit.

Increase your Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with firearms, ignore their loading property, and being within 5 feet of a hostile creature gives you no disadvantage on ranged attacks.

Your guard never quite drops. Add 5 to every initiative roll you make. While you are conscious no ambush catches you off guard, and an attacker hidden from your sight gets no advantage against you merely because you cannot see it.
Pick any three skills or tools, in any combination, and gain proficiency with each. This feat raises no ability score.
Once on each of your turns, when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can roll the weapon's damage dice a second time and keep whichever total you like.
You trace a warding sigil. Until the end of your next turn, bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from weapon attacks is halved against you.

Make a melee attack with the weapon you cast this through, against a creature within 5 feet. A hit deals the weapon's normal damage and wraps the target in booming energy until your next turn starts. Should the target move 5 feet or more of its own accord first, the energy discharges for 1d8 thunder damage and the spell ends.
You take control of a nonmagical flame within range that fills a 5-foot cube. You can expand it, extinguish it, double or halve its light, or make it form simple shapes and animations for an hour.

Flames rise from a 5-foot cube of ground within your view. Any creature standing there when it ignites, or ending its turn in it, makes a Dexterity saving throw or takes 1d8 fire damage. Unattended flammable objects in the cube catch alight.

Strike a creature within 5 feet with the weapon you cast this through. On a hit the weapon does its usual work, and emerald fire jumps from that target to one other creature you pick within 5 feet of it, burning the second for fire damage equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

You seize the air and push it. Choose one: a creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 5 feet, an unattended object weighing up to 5 pounds flies 10 feet, or you create a harmless sensory effect of wind.

Biting vermin boil over a creature you can see within range for a moment. Failing a Constitution saving throw costs it 1d6 poison damage and sends it stumbling 5 feet in a randomly determined direction, which can provoke opportunity attacks.

A lash of lightning snaps out at one creature within 15 feet. On a failed Strength saving throw the creature is dragged up to 10 feet straight toward you, and it takes 1d8 lightning damage if that leaves it within 5 feet.

Charge one, two or three pebbles at a touch. Thrown or slung by you or anyone you hand them to, each is a ranged spell attack dealing 1d6 bludgeoning damage plus your spellcasting ability modifier on a hit.

A shard of psychic force punches into the thoughts of one creature you can see within range. On a failed Intelligence saving throw it takes 1d6 psychic damage and, still reeling, subtracts 1d4 from its next saving throw made before your next turn ends.

You choose a 5-foot cube of loose earth within range and either excavate and move it, turn it into difficult terrain or smooth it flat for an hour, or reshape its colours and contours into shapes and words.
Your teeth lengthen, or your nails do, dripping acid. Make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet; a hit deals 1d10 acid damage. The change fades once the attack is resolved.
One creature you can see within range makes a Constitution saving throw. Failure drains the strength from its legs: 1d4 necrotic damage, and it drops prone.
You choose a 5-foot cube of water within range and either move it 5 feet, change its colour or opacity, form it into simple shapes, or freeze it solid provided no creature is inside.
You fling a spray of razor-edged conjured cards. Each creature in a 15-foot cone must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 slashing damage.
Spectral blades sweep outward around you for an instant. Every other creature within 5 feet takes 1d6 force damage unless it succeeds on a Dexterity saving throw.

A thorned vine lashes from your hand. Make a melee spell attack against a creature within range; on a hit it takes 1d6 piercing damage, and anything Large or smaller is hauled up to 10 feet toward you.

Point at a creature you can see within range and a funeral bell rings out around it. On a failed Wisdom saving throw it takes 1d8 necrotic damage, or 1d12 instead if it has already lost any hit points.
Burning light bursts out of you at a divine word. Each creature you single out within 5 feet takes 1d6 radiant damage unless it succeeds on a Constitution saving throw.

Some of the incoming energy is drawn into you rather than through you. The triggering damage type is halved against you until your next turn begins, and the first melee hit you land on your next turn carries an extra 1d6 damage of that same type.
Spectral frost sheathes you and your gear, granting 5 temporary hit points. Any creature that lands a melee attack on you while even one of those points remains suffers 5 cold damage.

Dark tendrils erupt from you and lash out. Each creature within 10 feet must make a Strength saving throw, taking 2d6 necrotic damage on a failure and half as much on a success. A creature that failed cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn.

You touch a beast with an Intelligence of 3 or lower and form a telepathic link with it. While the link holds you can perceive through its senses, it understands your simple commands, and you have advantage on attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of it.

One creature you can see within range is made to feel its own death coming. On a failed Wisdom saving throw it is frightened of you until the spell ends, with another save at the end of each of its turns. Constructs and undead feel nothing.

Make a ranged spell attack against a creature within range. On a hit, roll 2d8 and 1d6. The target takes damage equal to the total, of a type set by the lower of the two d8s: 1 acid, 2 cold, 3 fire, 4 force, 5 lightning, 6 poison, 7 psychic, 8 thunder. If the two d8s match, the energy leaps to a different creature within 30 feet of the target and you make a new attack roll against it, continuing as long as the dice keep matching and there are new targets.

You throw a 4-inch sphere of raw energy at a creature you can see within range. Pick acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison or thunder as the orb forms, then make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit the target takes 3d8 damage of the type you picked.

You challenge a creature you can see within range to fight you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be drawn to you: while the spell lasts it has disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone but you, and it must make a Wisdom saving throw to move more than 30 feet away from you. The spell ends if you attack anyone else, cast a harmful spell on anyone else, or end your turn more than 30 feet from the target.

The ground bucks in a 10-foot radius around you. Every other creature there makes a Dexterity saving throw, falling prone and taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage on a failure. Any loose earth caught in the radius becomes difficult terrain.
A willing creature you touch reacts faster than it should. While the spell lasts it rolls an extra 1d8 and adds it to every initiative roll it makes.

The next time you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack while this spell is active, thorns explode from the target. It and every creature within 5 feet of it must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 1d10 piercing damage on a failure and half as much on a success.

You lay a curse on a creature you can see within range. Until the spell ends, your attacks that hit the cursed creature deal an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. Name one ability when you cast the spell: the cursed creature has disadvantage on ability checks made with it. Should the creature drop to 0 hit points before the spell ends, you may spend a bonus action on a later turn of yours to move the curse to another creature. A remove curse spell cast on the creature ends the spell early.

Gravity doubles in a 10-foot-radius sphere within range. Each creature there makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 force damage on a failure and having its speed halved until the end of your next turn, or half damage on a success.
You force a creature within range to move at your word. On a failed Wisdom saving throw it moves up to half its speed in a direction you choose, and can be made to drop what it is holding.

A sudden stab of doubt unsettles the creature that just succeeded. It rerolls the d20 and must keep the lower of the two results. You then pass the stolen confidence to any creature you can see within range, which gains advantage on one attack roll, ability check or saving throw made within the next minute.

You weave a hidden trap into a 5-foot square of floor. The first Large or smaller creature to enter it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be magically hoisted into the air, restrained and hanging upside down, until it or another creature escapes with a successful Arcana check or the rope is cut.
A wave of alertness rolls out from you. Each creature you choose within 30 feet immediately wakes, stands up from prone at no movement cost, and is freed from magical sleep.

A stream of acid sprays out in a 30-foot line, 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be covered in acid, taking 2d4 acid damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use its action to scrape the acid off itself or another creature, ending the effect on that creature.

The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack while this spell is active, the attack deals an extra 2d6 thunder damage and the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away and knocked prone.

You touch the ground and call on the wisdom of the wild. You learn one useful fact about the surrounding half mile of your choosing: where to find food and water, the safest path, tracks of a creature type, or the nearest shelter.

A beam of crackling energy lances toward a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack; on a hit the target takes 1d12 lightning damage and the beam remains connected. On each of your later turns you can use your action to deal 1d12 lightning damage automatically, and the spell ends if the target moves more than 30 feet away or gains total cover.

The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack while this spell is active, the attack deals an extra 1d6 psychic damage. The target must then succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of you until the spell ends. A frightened target can spend its action on a Wisdom check against your spell save DC to end the effect on itself.

The air carries you. Until the spell ends your movement never provokes opportunity attacks, and once during that time you may claim advantage on a single weapon attack roll, adding 1d8 force damage on a hit and 30 feet of speed for the rest of that turn.
Roaring flame erupts from you along a line 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. Every creature caught in it makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d8 fire damage on a failure and half as much on a success.

You touch a willing beast and, for the duration, perceive through its senses as well as your own. You can use your action to see and hear through the beast instead of yourself, gaining any special senses it has; while you do, you are blind and deaf to your own surroundings.
Pick one skill. You are proficient in it for the duration, the training surfacing as though remembered from a life that was not yours.
Spinning daggers fill a 5-foot cube centred on a point within range. Entering the cube for the first time in a turn, or beginning a turn inside it, costs a creature 4d4 slashing damage.

You plant four pieces of nonmagical ammunition in the ground and ward the area around them. Until the spell ends, whenever a creature other than you comes within 30 feet of the ammunition for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there, one piece flies up to strike it: the creature makes a Dexterity saving throw or takes 1d6 piercing damage, and that piece of ammunition is spent.

One humanoid you can see within range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed. While charmed it must use its action before moving each turn to make a melee attack against a creature other than itself that you choose. It can make a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.

A whirlwind of swirling dust fills a 5-foot cube within range. A creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of it must make a Strength saving throw, taking 1d8 bludgeoning damage and being pushed 10 feet on a failure. As a bonus action you can move the dust devil 30 feet.

Bands of yellow force loop around a creature you can see within range. Failing a Strength saving throw drops its flying speed to 0, and it sinks 60 feet each round until it reaches the ground or the spell ends.

You bless a willing creature with luck. Once before the spell ends it can roll an additional d20 on an attack roll, ability check or saving throw and use either result, or force an attacker to reroll against it.

You rewrite the last 6 seconds of a conversation. Every creature that heard you remembers you saying something else of your choosing, provided it is not obviously false, and you gain advantage on a Charisma check made in the same exchange.

A nature spirit appears in a 5-foot cube within range. When a creature enters that space on its turn or starts its turn there, you can use your reaction to have the spirit restore 1d6 hit points to it. The spirit can heal a number of times equal to 1 + your spellcasting ability modifier before it vanishes, and you can move it 30 feet as a bonus action.

You touch an object weighing no more than 10 pounds and fix it in place. Nothing can move it unless a creature succeeds on a Strength check against your spell save DC, and casting the spell with a higher slot makes it hold far more weight and last far longer.
You gain supernatural grace. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, you can move through other creatures' spaces, and your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

A Medium hand of earth rises from the ground and reaches for a creature within range. On a failed Strength saving throw the target takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and is restrained. As a bonus action you can move the hand to crush a restrained target for 2d6 more.

Draconic mischief fills a 20-foot cube within range. Roll on a table of effects each round: rainbow bubbles that impose disadvantage, a smell that provokes Constitution saves against poisoning, giggling fits that force Wisdom saves against incapacitation, or grasping tentacles of light that force Dexterity saves against being knocked prone.

You consume a nonmagical flame within range and choose an effect. Fireworks burst in a 10-foot radius, blinding creatures that fail a Constitution saving throw until the end of your next turn; or thick smoke fills a 20-foot radius, heavily obscuring it for a minute.

You weave shadow into a blade in your hand. It counts as a simple melee weapon with finesse, light and thrown (range 20/60), deals 2d8 psychic damage on a hit, and grants advantage on attacks against a target in dim light or darkness. If you drop it or throw it, it dissipates at the end of the turn and you can re-form it as a bonus action.
Cloud shapes itself into writing of up to ten words across a stretch of sky you can see. Anyone beneath it can read the message, and it holds until the spell ends.

Magical snowballs burst outward through a 5-foot-radius sphere around a point you pick within range. Each creature inside makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d6 cold damage on a failure and half as much on a success.

You call a bestial spirit to an unoccupied space you can see within range. It takes an Air, Land or Water form of your choosing and acts on your turn, obeying your verbal commands. Its attack bonus and save DC match your own spellcasting numbers, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or the spell ends.

You psychically lash one creature you can see within range. It must make an Intelligence saving throw, taking 3d6 psychic damage on a failure and half as much on a success. On a failed save it also cannot take a reaction until the end of its next turn, and on that turn it must choose whether to move, take an action, or take a bonus action.
Pick a creature you can see and an unoccupied space you can see within range. The creature is transported there, though one that objects avoids the trip with a successful Constitution saving throw.

A strong wind howls in a 10-foot radius around you and moves with you. It deafens creatures in it, disperses gas and fog, extinguishes unprotected flames, makes the area difficult terrain for others, and gives ranged weapon attacks entering or leaving it disadvantage.

You invoke both death and life at a point within range. Each creature of your choice in a 10-foot radius must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d6 necrotic damage on a failure and half as much on a success. One creature of your choice in the area can then spend a Hit Die and regain that many hit points plus your spellcasting ability modifier.
A turn of the wrist sends an object you are holding into a pocket dimension. A bonus action calls it back to your hand from anywhere on the plane, and when the spell ends it drops at your feet.

Your body burns with fiery energy. Your speed increases by 20 feet, your movement never provokes opportunity attacks, and each creature you move within 5 feet of takes 1d6 fire damage, once per turn each.
A 30-foot radius of healing energy surrounds you and travels with you until the spell ends. Each turn, a bonus action lets you restore 2d6 hit points to any one creature inside it, yourself included.

The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack while this spell is active, the attack deals an extra 3d8 radiant damage and the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the spell ends. A blinded creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns.

You touch the minds of up to three willing creatures within range and they fall unconscious for the duration. When the spell ends or they take damage they wake, having gained the benefit of a short rest. A creature cannot benefit again until it finishes a long rest.

You throw a weapon or fire a piece of ammunition into the air and it becomes a cone of identical weapons that vanish on impact. Each creature in a 60-foot cone must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d8 damage of the weapon's type on a failure and half as much on a success.
A 30-foot aura of holy power spreads from you and travels with you. Until the spell ends, weapon hits by you and by every friendly creature inside it carry an extra 1d4 radiant damage.
Pick acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder. A nonmagical weapon you touch counts as magical for the duration, striking at +1 to hit and carrying an extra 1d4 damage of the type you named.

You reach into a creature's mind and stoke its paranoia. On a failed Intelligence saving throw it loses the ability to tell friend from foe, treating every creature it can see as an enemy until the spell ends. It repeats the save each time it takes damage.

Churned soil and stone fountain upward through a 20-foot cube within range. Each creature caught there makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d12 bludgeoning damage on a failure and half as much on a success, and the disturbed ground is left as difficult terrain.

A willing creature you touch falls into a cataleptic state indistinguishable from death. It is blinded and incapacitated, its speed drops to 0, and it has resistance to all damage but psychic. It is unaware of its surroundings and cannot be poisoned or diseased further while the spell lasts.
Charge a quiver you touch with fire. Each of the next twelve pieces of ammunition drawn from it adds 1d6 fire damage when it hits, and the spell ends once the twelfth leaves the quiver.
You summon a tiny courier creature and hand it an object of up to 10 pounds and a message. It vanishes and delivers both to a creature you name on the same plane, provided you have met them.

You open a 20-foot-radius sphere of cold void within range. It is filled with magical darkness that no light can dispel. A creature that starts its turn in the sphere takes 2d6 cold damage. A creature that ends its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 acid damage from unseen mouths.
Ward yourself or one willing creature within range. Until the spell ends, psychic damage against the warded mind is halved and it rolls Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saves with advantage.
You tear at your own vitality to knit someone else's. Take 4d8 necrotic damage, which nothing can reduce; one creature you can see within range recovers twice that many hit points.

The next time you make a ranged weapon attack while this spell is active, the ammunition becomes a bolt of lightning. On a hit the target takes 4d8 lightning damage instead of the weapon's normal damage, and half that on a miss. Either way, each creature within 10 feet of the target takes 2d8 lightning damage, halved on a successful Dexterity saving throw.

Six burning motes orbit you. Spend a bonus action to fling one or two at points up to 120 feet away; each detonates in a 5-foot radius for 2d6 fire damage, halved on a successful Dexterity saving throw.

You create intense pressure in a 30-foot cone and decide whether it pulls or pushes. Each creature there makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 6d6 force damage and being moved 15 feet on a failure, or half damage and no movement on a success.

A burst of cold energy fills a 30-foot cone. Each creature there must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 3d8 cold damage on a failure and being restrained by ice until it or another creature breaks it free with an action.

Spirits gather around you out to 10 feet. Until the spell ends, any enemy that starts its turn in that area has its speed reduced by 10 feet and cannot regain hit points. Once per turn, when you hit a creature within 10 feet with an attack, it takes an extra 1d8 radiant, necrotic or cold damage of your choice.

You call a fey spirit to an unoccupied space you can see within range. It takes a Fuming, Mirthful or Tricksy mood of your choosing and acts on your turn, obeying your verbal commands. Its attack bonus and save DC match your own spellcasting numbers, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or the spell ends.

You summon demons at random: either two of challenge rating 1 or lower, four of rating 1/2 or lower, or eight of rating 1/4 or lower. They are not under your control and attack the nearest creature that is not a demon.

You call a shadow spirit to an unoccupied space you can see within range. It takes a Fury, Despair or Fear emotion of your choosing and acts on your turn, obeying your verbal commands. Its attack bonus and save DC match your own spellcasting numbers, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or the spell ends.
You call an undead spirit to an unoccupied space you can see. You choose a Ghostly, Putrid or Skeletal form, and it acts on your turn using your spellcasting numbers.

You teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within range, and thunder cracks at both your origin and your destination. Each creature within 10 feet of the space you left takes 3d10 thunder damage, halved on a successful Constitution saving throw. You can bring one willing creature with you.

You conjure a wave of water 30 feet long, 10 feet wide and 10 feet tall. Each creature in its space must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d8 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failure, or half damage on a success. The water then spreads out and extinguishes open flames.
You touch a Tiny nonmagical object and animate it as a servant with its own senses and speed. It obeys your spoken commands, though it cannot attack, and drops lifeless when the spell ends.
A wall of swirling sand up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high and 10 feet thick rises from the ground. It blocks sight entirely, and a creature moving through it does so at half speed.

You conjure a wall of water up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high and 1 foot thick, or a ring 20 feet in diameter. Ranged weapon attacks passing through it have disadvantage, fire damage passing through is halved, and cold damage freezes it into difficult terrain.

A purifying aura of 30 feet radiates from you and moves with you. Friendly creatures in it, including you, cannot contract disease, have resistance to poison damage, have advantage on saves against effects that would blind, charm, deafen, frighten, paralyze, poison or stun, and have advantage on saves against other conditions.

You choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder and curse a creature within range. On a failed Constitution saving throw it loses resistance to that damage type, and the first time it takes that damage each turn it takes an extra 2d6.

You summon a loyal, intelligent spirit that takes the form of a griffon, pegasus, peryton, dire wolf, rhinoceros or saber-toothed tiger. It serves as a mount, shares your telepathic bond, and vanishes to a pocket of its own plane when it drops to 0 hit points, letting you resummon it later.
A tower of the size and style you choose rises from the ground, up to four storeys, furnished and stocked with food and light. Only those you name can enter.

You conjure a vine that sprouts from the ground at a point within range. As a bonus action on each of your turns you can direct it to lash at one creature within 30 feet of it, which must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be pulled up to 20 feet directly toward the vine.

A 20-foot-radius sphere of crushing force implodes at a point you choose. Each creature there must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 5d10 force damage and being pulled to the centre on a failure, or half damage and no movement on a success.

You take one of two forms. Primal Beast gives you a 10-foot speed bonus, darkvision to 120 feet, natural claws dealing an extra 1d6 force damage on a hit, and advantage on Strength checks and saves. Great Tree gives you 10 temporary hit points, advantage on Constitution saves, advantage on Dexterity and Wisdom-based attacks, and difficult terrain for enemies within 15 feet.

You unleash a spear of psychic energy at one creature you can see, or speak a name and strike whoever bears it within range even unseen. The target makes an Intelligence saving throw, taking 7d6 psychic damage on a failure and being incapacitated until the end of your next turn, or half damage on a success.

Guttering shadows wrap you and swallow the light nearby. Radiant damage against you is halved, attackers roll against you with disadvantage, and any creature landing a melee attack on you takes 2d8 necrotic damage in return.

Dim green light fills a 30-foot-radius sphere centred on a point you choose within range. A creature that enters the sphere or starts its turn there must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 4d10 radiant damage, gain a level of exhaustion, and shed dim light for the duration, unable to hide.

The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack while this spell is active, the attack deals an extra 4d6 psychic damage. The target must then succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks and be unable to take reactions until the end of its next turn.

A 20-foot-radius sphere of crackling storm appears at a point you choose. It is difficult terrain, and a creature that ends its turn there takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage on a failed Strength saving throw. As a bonus action you can call a lightning bolt at one creature within 60 feet of the sphere for 4d6 lightning damage, halved on a successful Dexterity save.

You call an aberrant spirit to an unoccupied space you can see within range. You choose a beholderkin, slaad or star spawn form, and it acts on your turn, obeying your verbal commands. Its attack bonus and save DC match your own spellcasting numbers, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or the spell ends.

You call a construct spirit to an unoccupied space you can see within range. You choose a clay, metal or stone body, and it acts on your turn, obeying your verbal commands. Its attack bonus and save DC match your own spellcasting numbers, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or the spell ends.

You call an elemental spirit to an unoccupied space you can see within range. You choose air, earth, fire or water, and it acts on your turn, obeying your verbal commands. Its attack bonus and save DC match your own spellcasting numbers, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or the spell ends.

You summon a demon of challenge rating 5 or lower. It obeys your commands while you concentrate, but it makes a Charisma saving throw at the end of each of your turns and breaks free on a success, attacking you before vanishing.

A 5-foot-radius sphere of water appears at a point you choose. Creatures in its space must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be restrained inside it, and as a bonus action you can move the sphere up to 30 feet, carrying anything it holds.

The next time you hit with a weapon attack while this spell is active, the attack deals an extra 5d10 force damage. If that leaves the target with 50 hit points or fewer, it is banished: a native of another plane is sent home permanently, and any other creature is held in harmless limbo until the spell ends.

Divine energy radiates from you in a 30-foot aura that moves with you. Friendly creatures in it, including you, have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and a creature that succeeds on a save for half damage takes no damage instead.

You fire a piece of ammunition or throw a weapon at a point within range and a volley of identical weapons rains down. Each creature in a 40-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d8 damage of the weapon's type on a failure and half as much on a success.

You take control of the air in a 100-foot cube within range, choosing gusts, a downdraft or an updraft. Gusts impose difficult terrain and disadvantage on ranged attacks against the wind, a downdraft knocks flying creatures down, and an updraft slows falls and lengthens jumps.

Dark filaments spear up to five Small or Medium corpses within range and haul them upright as skeletons or zombies under your command. They act on your turn, add your spellcasting ability modifier to attack and damage rolls, and collapse when the spell ends.

Sunlight fills a 30-foot-radius, 40-foot-tall cylinder centred on a point within range. A creature that enters the cylinder or starts its turn there must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 4d10 radiant damage on a failure and half as much on a success. You can move the cylinder 60 feet as a bonus action on each of your turns.

You strike the ground and a burst of divine energy ripples outward. Each creature you choose within 30 feet must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure it takes 5d6 thunder damage plus 5d6 radiant or necrotic damage, your choice, and is knocked prone. On a success it takes half as much damage and is not knocked prone.

A shadowy tendril reaches for a creature within range. It must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d8 necrotic damage on a success and ending the spell. On a failure the tendril latches on and deals 4d8 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns, healing you for half that amount.
Pick an unoccupied space you can see up to 60 feet away and appear in it. On any later turn of yours a bonus action repeats the jump, until the spell ends.

You imbue a weapon you touch with holy power. For the duration it emits bright light and deals an extra 2d8 radiant damage on a hit. You can end the spell early as a bonus action to make the weapon burst: each creature within 30 feet must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 4d8 radiant damage and being blinded for a minute on a failure, or half damage and no blindness on a success.

Flames wreathe one creature you can see within range. It must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 fire damage on a failure and half as much on a success. On a failure it burns for the duration, shedding bright light and taking 4d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns.
You summon a devil of challenge rating 6 or lower from the Nine Hells. It is not under your control and acts on its own, testing the limits of any bargain you strike with it while it remains.

A mass of swirling water appears in a 30-foot radius centred on a point you can see. It is difficult terrain, and a creature that enters it or starts its turn there must make a Strength saving throw or take 6d6 bludgeoning damage and be pulled 10 feet toward the centre.

You send ribbons of negative energy at a creature within range. Unless it is undead it makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 5d12 necrotic damage on a failure and half as much on a success; a humanoid killed by it rises as a zombie under your command. An undead target instead gains half that many temporary hit points.
Touch a willing creature and name a skill it is already proficient in. Until the spell ends its proficiency bonus counts double on ability checks made with that skill.

You flicker between up to five creatures you can see within range, striking each one. Make a melee spell attack against each target; on a hit it takes 6d10 force damage. You then teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of one of the targets.

You call a celestial spirit to an unoccupied space you can see. You choose an Avenger form that attacks at range or a Defender form that shields allies; it acts on your turn using your spellcasting numbers and can heal with its touch.

You call a draconic spirit to an unoccupied space you can see. You choose chromatic, metallic or gem, and it acts on your turn with your spellcasting numbers, flying, biting, and exhaling a breath weapon of its kind.
A quiver you touch refills itself faster than you can empty it. Each turn until the spell ends, a bonus action lets you attack twice with a weapon drawing ammunition from that quiver.

You choose a point within range and psychic energy bursts in a 20-foot radius. Each creature in the area that can think must make an Intelligence saving throw, taking 8d6 psychic damage on a failure and half as much on a success. A creature that failed also has muddled thoughts for a minute, subtracting 1d6 from its attack rolls, ability checks and Constitution saves for concentration.

You shunt the creature a moment out of time. On a failed Wisdom saving throw its attack or spell is wasted and it vanishes until the end of your next turn, returning to its space with no memory of the gap.

You choose a 40-foot cube of stone or mud within range. Stone becomes thick mud, making the area difficult terrain and restraining creatures that fail a Dexterity saving throw; mud becomes stone, trapping creatures that fail a save until they are freed.

A wall of brilliant light 60 feet long, 10 feet high and 5 feet thick springs up. A creature in its area when it appears takes 4d8 radiant damage and is blinded for a minute, halved and unblinded on a successful Constitution saving throw. As an action you can collapse the wall into a 60-foot beam for the same damage.

You rouse the natural world in a 60-foot cube. Trees lash at creatures you choose for 4d6 slashing damage, grasses and undergrowth restrain them, roots trip them, and loose rocks fly at them for 3d6 bludgeoning damage, each with its own saving throw.

You create two linked 10-foot-diameter rings of magic, one on a surface you can see within range and one on a surface you can see within 10 feet of yourself. Any creature or object entering one portal leaves through the other. As a bonus action on a later turn you can turn either portal to face a new direction.

You cause up to six pillars of stone, each 5 feet in diameter and up to 30 feet high, to burst from the ground at points you can see. A creature in a pillar's space is pushed aside or, if it cannot be, takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage when it is pinned against a ceiling, halved on a successful Dexterity saving throw.

You cut yourself with a jewelled dagger, taking 2d4 piercing damage that cannot be healed until the spell ends, and shape a homunculus servant. It obeys your commands, acts on your turn, and can deliver a bite that grants you temporary hit points drawn from the target.

You ward an area up to 90 feet on a side. You choose which creatures pass freely, and the rest face entangling plants, an alarm that only you hear, an illusion of thick woodland, and druidic guardians that lash at intruders.

A field of platinum light protects a creature you can see. It gains half cover, resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning and poison damage, and takes no damage on a successful Dexterity save for half. As a bonus action you can move the field to another creature within 60 feet.

A crack of gravitational energy opens along a 100-foot line, 5 feet wide. Each creature in it makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 8d8 force damage on a failure and half on a success; creatures within 10 feet of the line are pulled toward it and take the same damage if they fail.

Flames wreathe your body for the duration. You are immune to fire damage and resistant to cold, you shed bright light, any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you takes 1d10 fire damage, and as an action you can create a 15-foot line of fire for 4d8 fire damage, halved on a successful Dexterity saving throw.

Frost covers your body for the duration. You are immune to cold damage and resistant to fire, ice spreads from you in a 10-foot radius as difficult terrain, and as an action you can exhale a 15-foot cone of freezing wind for 4d6 cold damage and halved speed, with a Constitution saving throw for half damage and no slowing.

Bits of rock cover your body for the duration. You have resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, you can move through solid earth as if it were difficult terrain, and as an action you can shake the ground in a 15-foot radius, knocking creatures prone on a failed Dexterity saving throw.

Wind swirls around you for the duration. Ranged weapon attacks against you have disadvantage, you gain a flying speed of 60 feet, and as an action you can create a 15-foot cube of whirling wind that deals 2d10 bludgeoning damage on a failed Constitution saving throw, half on a success.

You trap a creature in an illusory cage of its own worst memories. On a failed Intelligence saving throw it takes 5d10 psychic damage and is restrained, perceiving itself surrounded by a hazard only it can see. When the spell ends it takes 10d10 psychic damage.

Acid, cold, fire, lightning and thunder damage are all halved against you for the duration. Taking damage of one of those types, you may spend a reaction to shed every resistance in exchange for outright immunity to that one type until your next turn ends.

The air crackles with teleportation magic. You choose up to five creatures you can see within range and teleport each one up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. An unwilling creature can resist with a Wisdom saving throw.

You snatch the departing soul and trap it in your cage, preventing it being raised. While you hold it you can spend one of its five charges to heal yourself 2d8, gain advantage on a roll, ask the soul a question, steal a glimpse through its eyes, or add 2d8 to a necromancy spell's damage.

You call a fiendish spirit to an unoccupied space you can see. You choose a Demon, Devil or Yugoloth form, and it acts on your turn using your spellcasting numbers, obeying your commands while you concentrate.

You draw on the Lower or Upper Planes. Either way you are immune to fire and poison or to radiant and necrotic damage, cannot be charmed or frightened, gain a flying speed of 40 feet, add your spellcasting modifier to your AC, and can attack twice with weapons or cantrips.

You channel magic into fighting prowess. You gain 50 temporary hit points, advantage on attack rolls with simple and martial weapons, an extra attack with the Attack action, proficiency with martial weapons and Constitution saves, and an extra 2d12 force damage on weapon hits. You cannot cast spells while transformed, and when the spell ends you suffer a level of exhaustion.

Seven star-like motes circle your head, shedding bright light. As a bonus action you can hurl one at a creature within 120 feet, making a ranged spell attack for 4d12 radiant damage on a hit. When four or fewer motes remain the spell no longer sheds light.
You take on draconic aspects: blindsight out to 30 feet, a 60-foot flying speed, and an action to exhale a 60-foot cone dealing 6d8 force damage, halved on a successful Dexterity saving throw.
You and up to eight willing creatures fall into a shared dream and wake on another world you have seen depicted, arriving in an unoccupied space of that world's choosing.

You consecrate a temple up to 120 feet on a side. Fiends and undead cannot enter, its doors open only for those you name, and you can add wards such as bright light, a bell that only you hear, and healing for those who rest inside.
You bind the life force of two creatures within range. While tethered, damage or healing to one is mirrored onto the other, and the spell ends if either drops to 0 hit points.

A cyclone 10 feet in radius and 30 feet high roars into being at a point you choose. A creature entering it or starting its turn there must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d6 bludgeoning damage on a failure, and a failed Strength save leaves it restrained and lifted inside the whirlwind.

You draw the moisture out of every creature in a 30-foot cube within range. Each one must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 12d8 necrotic damage on a failure and half as much on a success. Constructs and undead are unaffected, and plants and water elementals have disadvantage on the save.

A 40-foot-radius sphere of crushing darkness appears, blocking all light and even darkvision, and silencing sound within it. A creature that starts its turn there takes 8d10 force damage, halved on a successful Constitution saving throw, and a creature reduced to 0 hit points there is disintegrated.

A shadowy Huge dragon rises from a point you choose. Creatures that see it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for a minute. As an action you can have it breathe at a 60-foot cone, dealing 7d6 damage of a type you chose when casting, halved on a successful Intelligence saving throw.

Magical darkness fills a 60-foot-radius sphere within range, blocking even darkvision and other light. Shrieking, howling voices sound inside it, and each creature that starts its turn there takes 8d8 psychic damage, halved on a successful Wisdom saving throw.

A square keep of stone 120 feet on a side pushes up out of the ground where you choose, courtyard and furnishings included. Unseen servants keep house in it, and it stands for seven days unless dispelled.

You shatter a creature's perception of reality. While it fails its Wisdom saving throws it cannot take reactions and is blinded to the true world, and on each of your turns you roll to hurl it through a random plane, dealing bludgeoning, psychic, cold, fire, force or lightning damage of 6d12 or more.

A mental channel opens between you and one willing creature you know well, anywhere on your current plane. Words, images, sounds and other sensations pass along it freely in both directions, distance no object.

You tear open a rift in the shape of a sword. A bonus action moves it up to 30 feet and swings it twice as melee spell attacks, 4d12 force damage each. It crits on a roll of 18 or higher, and a crit trebles its damage dice rather than doubling them.

You transform up to ten creatures you can see within range. An unwilling target can resist with a Wisdom saving throw. Each new form must be a beast whose challenge rating is no higher than the target's, and a transformed creature drops back to its own form when its temporary hit points run out.

You unleash psychic power at up to ten creatures you can see within range. Each must make an Intelligence saving throw, taking 14d6 psychic damage and being stunned on a failure, or half damage and no stunning on a success. A stunned creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, taking 3d6 psychic damage on each failure. A creature killed by this spell has its head explode.

A 20-foot-radius sphere of devastating gravity appears. Nonmagical objects there are destroyed, creatures within 100 feet are pulled toward it, and a creature in the sphere is restrained and takes 5d10 force damage at the start of each of its turns.

You age a creature you can see within range. On a failed Constitution saving throw it takes 10d12 necrotic damage and ages to the point of dying of old age within days, its Dexterity dropping and its frailty visible. Greater restoration or a wish can undo it.

Choose one creature that is not hostile to you. Until the spell ends you have advantage on every Charisma check you make against it. When the spell ends the creature knows its goodwill was worked on by magic and turns hostile toward you: a creature given to violence may attack you, and a subtler one looks for another way to get even, as the GM decides.

You conduct one of six sacred rites, chosen as you begin the hour. Each needs a willing target you touch during the rite.

**Atonement.** Touch a creature whose alignment has changed. You make a DC 20 Wisdom (Insight) check; on a success you know whether its wish to return is sincere, and if it is, the spell restores its former alignment.

**Bless Water.** Touch a flask holding up to a pint of water. It becomes holy water.

**Coming of Age.** Touch a humanoid entering adulthood. Once within the next 24 hours, when it makes an ability check, it can roll a d4 and add the result. A creature can receive this rite once in its life.

**Dedication.** Touch a humanoid who wishes to devote itself to your deity. Once within the next 24 hours, when it makes a saving throw, it can roll a d4 and add the result. A creature can receive this rite once.

**Funeral.** Touch a corpse that has been dead no longer than a day. For the next 7 days it cannot become undead by any means short of a wish spell.

**Wedding.** Touch two adult humanoids willing to be bound to each other. For the next 7 days each has a +2 bonus to AC while within 30 feet of the other. A creature can receive this rite again only after its partner has died.

A 30-foot radius of sheltering life force surrounds you and moves with you until the spell ends. Each creature in it that is not hostile to you, yourself included, has resistance to necrotic damage and cannot have its hit point maximum reduced. Such a creature that is alive and begins its turn in the aura at 0 hit points regains 1 hit point.

You murmur a jarring strain that only one creature of your choice within range can hear. It must make a Wisdom saving throw, taking 3d6 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failure it must also spend its reaction, if it has one, to move as far as its speed allows away from you, by a route that avoids obvious danger such as fire or a pit. A deafened creature succeeds on the save automatically.

A willing creature you touch gains a dragon's breath. Pick acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison. Until the spell ends, the creature can use its action to exhale a 15-foot cone of that energy; each creature in the cone must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d6 damage of the chosen type on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The next time a weapon attack of yours hits a creature before the spell ends, thorned vines burst from the wound and grasp it. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be restrained by the vines until the spell ends; a Large or larger creature has advantage on the save, and on a success the vines wither away. While restrained this way it takes 1d6 piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. The target, or a creature that can reach it, can use an action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC, tearing the vines away on a success.

You fling a sliver of ice at one creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against it; on a hit it takes 1d10 piercing damage. Hit or miss, the sliver then bursts: the target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 cold damage.

You drive a shard of thought into the mind of one creature you can see within range. It must make a Wisdom saving throw, taking 3d8 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failure you also know where it is for as long as the spell lasts and you share a plane with it: it cannot hide from you, and being invisible gives it no benefit against you.

You plant an illusion in the mind of a creature you can see within range, which must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure you shape a phantasm of your choosing, an object, a creature or some other visible thing no larger than a 10-foot cube, that only the target perceives. The target believes in it and explains away anything that does not fit; it can spend its action on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to see the illusion for what it is. While it believes, a phantasm that could plausibly hurt it, such as a beast or a blaze, deals it 1d6 psychic damage on each of your turns that it spends in the phantasm's space or within 5 feet of it, and the target perceives that damage as whatever kind the illusion suggests.

The next time you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack while this spell is active, your weapon blazes white-hot: the attack deals an extra 1d6 fire damage and sets the target alight. At the start of each of its turns until the spell ends, the burning target makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 1d6 fire damage on a failure and ending the spell on a success. The spell also ends if the target or a creature within 5 feet of it spends an action to put out the flames, or if something else douses them.

A wall of water up to 300 feet long, 300 feet high and 50 feet thick rises at a point you choose within range and lasts for the duration. Each creature in its area when it appears must make a Strength saving throw, taking 6d10 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. At the start of each of your turns afterward the wall, with everything caught in it, rolls 50 feet away from you; any Huge or smaller creature inside it, or whose space it enters, must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take 5d10 bludgeoning damage, no more than once a round. At the end of each such turn the wall loses 50 feet of height and that later damage drops by 1d10, and the spell ends when the wall reaches 0 feet. A creature caught inside moves only by swimming, and only after a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC; one that leaves the wall falls to the ground.

A foot-wide globe of green acid streaks to a point you choose within range and bursts in a 20-foot-radius sphere. Each creature there must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save it takes 10d4 acid damage, and another 5d4 acid damage at the end of its next turn. On a successful save it takes half the first damage and none at the end of its next turn.

A word of healing floods the creature you touch, restoring all of its hit points. If it is charmed, frightened, paralyzed or stunned, that condition ends, and if it is prone it can use its reaction to stand up. Undead and constructs are unaffected.
A barbarian whose rage becomes a frenzy: an extra attack while raging, immunity to fear and charm, and a presence that cows enemies.
A bard who collects knowledge from every discipline, cutting enemies down with words and borrowing spells from any class list.
A cleric of healing and vitality, whose cures restore more, whose armor is heavy, and whose domain spells are always prepared.
A druid attuned to one kind of terrain, with bonus spells drawn from it, an extra cantrip and slots recovered on a short rest.
A fighter of raw physical prowess: critical hits on a 19, remarkable athletics and a second fighting style.
A monk who masters unarmed combat, knocking foes down and away with every flurry and healing with ki.
A paladin sworn to honesty, courage and compassion, with a sacred weapon and protection from fiends and undead.
A ranger who studies prey and picks a fighting technique to bring down hordes or giants.
A rogue of quick hands and quick feet: faster climbing, items used as a bonus action, and stealth on the move.
A sorcerer whose magic comes from a dragon ancestor: tougher scales, an elemental affinity and, in time, wings.
A warlock whose patron is a fiend of the lower planes, granting fiery spells and temporary hit points on a kill.
A wizard who shapes destructive magic, sculpting spells around allies and making cantrips hit harder.
Add your Charisma modifier to the damage of each Eldritch Blast beam. Usually the first invocation a warlock takes.
Cast mage armor on yourself at will, without a spell slot.
Cast levitate on yourself at will, without a spell slot.
You no longer need to sleep and cannot be forced to. You keep watch through the whole night.
Cast speak with animals at will, without a spell slot.
You gain proficiency in Deception and Persuasion.
Cast compulsion once per long rest using a warlock spell slot.
Inscribe two 1st-level rituals in your Book of Shadows and cast them as rituals. You can add more rituals you find.
Cast hold monster at will on a celestial, fiend or elemental, without a slot, once per creature per long rest.
A bonus action wraps you in buzzing flies for a minute: advantage on Intimidation, disadvantage on other Charisma checks, and poison damage to creatures that end their turn within 5 feet.
You see normally in darkness, magical and nonmagical, out to 120 feet. Pairs famously with casting darkness on yourself.
Cast confusion once per long rest using a warlock spell slot.
You have advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration on a spell.
Cast detect magic at will, without a spell slot.
Your Eldritch Blast reaches 300 feet instead of 120.
Cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, without a slot.
Touch a willing humanoid and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn, extendable each turn.
As an action, see through solid objects out to 30 feet for a minute, once per short or long rest.
You can breathe underwater, gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed, and cast water breathing once per long rest without a slot.
Whenever you regain hit points while your familiar is within 100 feet, you regain the maximum possible.
Once per turn when Eldritch Blast hits, you can pull the target 10 feet toward you.
Your pact weapon counts as magical, gives +1 to attack and damage, and can serve as your spellcasting focus. You can also make a bow or crossbow your pact weapon.
Your familiar gains a flying or swimming speed, its attacks count as magical, it can be commanded as a bonus action, and it can impose your spell save DC on its effects.
Your pact weapon deals extra necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier on a hit.
A bonus action deals psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier to your hex target and every creature within 5 feet of it.
Cast disguise self at will, without a spell slot.
Cast alter self at will, without a spell slot.
Cast conjure elemental once per long rest using a warlock spell slot.
Cast slow once per long rest using a warlock spell slot.
Cast silent image at will, without a spell slot.
In dim light or darkness, become invisible as an action until you move or act.
Cast jump on yourself at will, without a spell slot.
The wearer of your talisman can add a d4 to a failed saving throw, a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest.
When the wearer of your talisman is hit, you can use a reaction to deal psychic damage equal to your proficiency bonus and push the attacker 10 feet.
A bonus action teleports you up to 30 feet to a space near your cursed target.
Once per turn when Eldritch Blast hits, you can push the target 10 feet away. Excellent battlefield control.
Cast polymorph once per long rest using a warlock spell slot.
Cast invisibility at will, without a spell slot.
Cast bestow curse once per long rest using a warlock spell slot.
Cast bane once per long rest using a warlock spell slot.
You attack twice with your pact weapon whenever you take the Attack action.
As a reaction on taking damage, encase yourself in ice for temporary hit points, at the cost of being restrained and taking cold damage; once per short or long rest.
Cast freedom of movement on yourself once per long rest, without a slot.
Cast arcane eye at will, without a spell slot.
You can speak through your familiar, perceive through its senses, and communicate with it at any distance on the same plane.
Cast speak with dead at will, without a spell slot.
You see the true form of any shapechanger or creature concealed by illusion within 30 feet.
You can conjure a magical weapon of any kind as an action, and it counts as magical. This is the melee warlock's pact.
You learn find familiar and can take special forms such as an imp, quasit, pseudodragon or sprite, and your familiar can attack with its own reaction.
You gain a Book of Shadows holding three cantrips from any class's list, which you can cast at will.
You gain an amulet that lets its wearer add a d4 to a failed ability check, a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest.
Spend a die to add it to a Stealth check or an initiative roll.
Spend a die to swap places with a willing ally within 5 feet, and one of you adds the die to your AC until your next turn.
As a reaction when a creature moves into your reach, spend a die to attack it and add the die to the damage.
Give up one of your attacks and spend a die to let an ally use their reaction to attack, adding the die to their damage.
Spend a die to add it to an Intimidation, Performance or Persuasion check.
Spend a die to add it to the damage and force a Strength save, dropping one item the target is holding.
Spend a die to add it to the damage and give the next attacker advantage against the target.
Spend a die and add it to your AC while you move.
A bonus action feints at a creature within 5 feet, giving you advantage on your next attack against it and adding the die to the damage.
Spend a die to add it to the damage and force a Wisdom save, giving the target disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you.
After hitting, spend a die as a bonus action to attempt a grapple, adding the die to your check.
Spend a die to reach 5 feet further with a melee attack and add the die to the damage.
Spend a die to add it to the damage and let an ally move half their speed without provoking from the target.
Spend a die to add it to the damage and frighten the target on a failed Wisdom save.
As a reaction, spend a die to reduce melee damage to you by the die plus your Dexterity modifier.
Spend a die to add it to an attack roll, before or after seeing whether it hits.
Spend a die to add it to the damage and push a Large or smaller target 15 feet on a failed Strength save.
A bonus action draws and throws a weapon, spending a die to add it to the damage.
A bonus action grants an ally temporary hit points equal to the die plus your Charisma modifier.
As a reaction when a creature misses you in melee, spend a die to attack it and add the die to the damage.
After hitting, spend a die to deal that much damage to a second creature within 5 feet of the first.
Spend a die to add it to a History, Insight or Investigation check.
Spend a die to add it to the damage and knock a Large or smaller target prone on a failed Strength save.
Spend 1 sorcery point to let a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier automatically succeed on the spell's saving throw.
Spend 1 sorcery point to double a spell's range, or give a touch spell 30 feet of reach.
Spend 1 sorcery point to reroll damage dice equal to your Charisma modifier.
Spend 1 sorcery point to double a spell's duration, up to 24 hours.
Spend 3 sorcery points to give one target disadvantage on its first saving throw against the spell.
Spend 2 sorcery points to cast a one-action spell as a bonus action instead.
Spend 2 sorcery points to reroll a missed attack roll for a spell.
Spend 1 sorcery point to cast without verbal or somatic components, which no one can see or hear you do.
Spend 1 sorcery point to change a spell's damage type among acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison and thunder.
Spend sorcery points equal to the spell's level to have a single-target spell hit a second creature.
Armor that raises the wearer's speed by 5 feet, grants a returning gauntlet attack, and replaces missing limbs.
Armor that lets the wearer use Intelligence for Strength checks and saves, and spend charges to add to a save or avoid being knocked prone.
Boots that let the wearer teleport back to a space they occupied earlier in the turn.
A focus granting +1 to spell attack rolls and letting spells ignore half cover.
Armor or a shield with a +1 bonus to AC, rising to +2 at higher levels.
A weapon with a +1 bonus to attack and damage, rising to +2 at higher levels.
A helm granting advantage on initiative rolls.
A tiny construct companion that acts on your turn, scouts, and channels your spells.
A garment with charges that turn a failed concentration save into a success.
A weapon that sheds light, grants +1 to attack and damage, and can blind an attacker as a reaction.
A ranged weapon with +1 to attack and damage that produces its own ammunition.
Reproduce a common magic item from the artificer's replicable list; the list grows with your level.
A shield with +1 AC and charges that push an attacker 15 feet away.
Armor granting resistance to one damage type of your choice.
A thrown weapon with +1 to attack and damage that flies back to the wielder's hand.
A ring that restores one expended spell slot of 3rd level or lower once per day.
Advantage on Sleight of Hand and Deception. Invoke it as a reaction to redirect an attack from one creature to another within 30 feet.
Doubled proficiency on tool checks. Invoke it on a hit for extra fire damage and to bind the target in fiery chains, restraining it.
Advantage on Animal Handling and Intimidation. Invoke it for a bonus to Strength and Constitution checks and saves for 10 minutes.
Advantage on saving throws against poison and resistance to poison damage. Invoke it to gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage for a minute.
Advantage on Insight and darkvision to 120 feet. Invoke it as a reaction to charm a creature within 30 feet that fails a Wisdom save.
Advantage on Arcana and you cannot be surprised while conscious. Invoke it to see glimpses of the future, granting advantage or imposing disadvantage on rolls near you.
Spend 6 ki to cast cone of cold.
Spend 3 ki to cast hold person.

As an action within 30 feet: a harmless sensory effect of an element, light or snuff a candle, torch or small campfire, chill or warm up to a pound of nonliving material for up to an hour, or shape earth, fire, water or mist that fits in a 1-foot cube into a crude form for a minute.
Spend 5 ki to cast stoneskin on yourself.
Spend 1 ki when you take the Attack action to add 10 feet of reach and fire damage to your unarmed strikes.
Spend 2 ki to strike a creature within 30 feet for 3d10 bludgeoning damage, pushing and knocking it prone on a failed Strength save.
Spend 4 ki to cast gaseous form on yourself.
Spend 4 ki to cast fly on yourself.
Spend 5 ki to cast wall of fire.
Spend 2 ki to cast gust of wind.
Spend 1 ki to freeze, thaw or reshape a 30-foot area of water or ice.
Spend 2 ki to cast burning hands.
Spend 2 ki to lash a creature within 30 feet for 3d10 bludgeoning damage, then pull it 25 feet or knock it prone on a failed Dexterity save.
Spend 6 ki to cast wall of stone.
Once per turn, a weapon hit on a creature already below its hit point maximum deals an extra 1d8 damage.
When a Large or larger creature within 5 feet hits or misses you with an attack, your reaction makes an attack against it right after.
Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature within 5 feet of the first target and in range.
Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.
After a creature hits you with an attack, you gain +4 AC against all its later attacks this turn.
Advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
As an action, a ranged weapon attack against any number of creatures within 10 feet of a point you can see in range, with a separate attack roll for each.
As an action, a melee attack against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each.
On a Dexterity save for half damage, you take none on a success and half on a failure.
When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, your reaction can make it repeat the attack against another creature of your choice.
When an attacker you can see hits you with an attack, your reaction halves the attack's damage against you.
A barbarian who takes a beast as a spirit guide, borrowing its strengths in and out of a rage.
Ritual casting of beast sense and speak with animals.

Choose a totem, whose gift holds while you rage: Bear gives resistance to all damage but psychic; Eagle gives other creatures disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you and lets you Dash as a bonus action; Elk raises your walking speed by 15 feet; Tiger adds 10 feet to your long jump and 3 feet to your high jump; Wolf gives your allies advantage on melee attacks against any hostile creature within 5 feet of you.

A lasting gift from your totem: Bear doubles your carrying capacity and gives advantage on Strength checks to push, pull, lift or break; Eagle lets you see clearly up to a mile away, and dim light no longer hampers your Perception; Elk doubles the travel pace of you and up to ten companions within 60 feet of you; Tiger makes you proficient in two of Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth and Survival; Wolf lets you track at a fast pace and move stealthily at a normal pace.
