As a bonus action, transform for a minute, a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest: you gain 1d10 + your warlock level temporary hit points and immunity to being frightened, and once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can make it save on Wisdom against your spell save DC or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

You no longer need to eat, drink or breathe. Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and roll damage, you can make that damage necrotic, and while in Form of Dread you roll one additional damage die.

You have resistance to necrotic damage, and immunity to it while in Form of Dread. When you are reduced to 0 hit points, a reaction drops you to 1 hit point instead, and each creature of your choice within 30 feet takes 2d10 + your warlock level necrotic damage; you then gain a level of exhaustion. You can use the reaction again only after 1d4 long rests.

As an action, once per long rest, project your spirit from your body for up to an hour (concentration) while the body lies unconscious. Your spirit carries copies of your gear; you resist bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage; your conjuration and necromancy spells need no verbal or somatic components, nor material ones without a cost; you can fly at your walking speed and hover, passing through creatures and objects as difficult terrain (1d10 force damage if you end a turn inside one); and while in Form of Dread, once on each of your turns when you deal necrotic damage, you regain hit points equal to half of it.
A pact with a deathless being that has cheated the grave and shares the trick.

You learn spare the dying. An undead that targets you directly with an attack or a harmful spell must first make a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or choose another target or lose the attack or spell; this doesn't protect you from area effects, and an undead that succeeds, or that you target with an attack or harmful spell, is immune for 24 hours. You have advantage on saving throws against disease.
Regain 1d8 + your Constitution modifier hit points when you succeed on a death save or stabilize a creature; recharges on a long rest.

You can hold your breath indefinitely and need no food, water or sleep (you still rest to recover from exhaustion and benefit from short and long rests), and you age at a tenth of the normal rate, immune to magical aging.
A bonus action heals 1d8 + your warlock level and reattaches severed body parts; recharges on a short or long rest.
A wizard who specializes in wards and counters, carrying a rechargeable magical shield.
Copying abjuration spells into your book costs half the time and gold.

Casting an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher raises a ward with hit points equal to twice your wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier, which absorbs damage aimed at you and recharges as you cast.
A reaction makes your Arcane Ward absorb damage aimed at a creature within 30 feet.
Add your proficiency bonus to ability checks made as part of an abjuration spell, such as counterspell and dispel magic.
Advantage on saves against spells, and resistance to damage from spells.
A wizard who makes things appear: objects, allies, and themselves somewhere safer.
Copying conjuration spells into your book costs half the time and gold.
An action conjures a nonmagical object up to 3 feet on a side and 10 pounds for an hour.
Teleport 30 feet or swap places with a willing creature; recharges on a long rest or when you cast a conjuration spell.
Concentration on a conjuration spell cannot be broken by taking damage.
Creatures you summon get 30 temporary hit points.
A wizard who reads the future well enough to swap out the dice they do not like.
Copying divination spells into your book costs half the time and gold.
Roll two d20s after each long rest and replace any attack, check or save made by you or a creature you can see with one of them; three dice from 14th level.
When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher with a spell slot, you regain one expended slot of a lower level than that spell, and no higher than 5th.

As an action, once per short or long rest, gain one of these until you are incapacitated or take a short or long rest: darkvision out to 60 feet, sight of the Ethereal Plane to 60 feet, the ability to read any language, or sight of invisible creatures and objects within 10 feet.
You roll three Portent dice after each long rest instead of two.
A wizard who works on minds: charm, compulsion, and making an enemy forget which side they are on.
Copying enchantment spells into your book costs half the time and gold.

As an action, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet: if it can see or hear you, it makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or is charmed by you until the end of your next turn, with speed 0 and incapacitated, and later actions extend it. It ends if you move more than 5 feet away, if it can't see or hear you, or if it takes damage. Once you use it on a creature, whatever the result, you can't use it on that creature again until you finish a long rest.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll against you, a reaction makes it save on Wisdom against your spell save DC or target the creature closest to it (other than you or itself) instead, deciding before you know whether the attack hits. If it succeeds, you can't use this on it again until you finish a long rest; it fails against creatures immune to being charmed.
An enchantment spell of 1st level or higher that targets one creature can target a second.
A charmed creature forgets it was charmed, and you can strip up to your Charisma modifier plus one hour of memory on a failed save.
A wizard who wins by making the battlefield disagree with everyone else's senses.
Copying illusion spells into your book costs half the time and gold.
You know minor illusion and can create sound and an image with the same casting.
When you cast an illusion spell with a duration of a minute or longer, you can use your action to change the nature of that illusion, within the spell's normal limits, as long as you can see it.
A reaction interposes an illusory duplicate so an attack that would hit you misses; recharges on a short or long rest.
A bonus action makes one object in your illusion real for a minute.
A wizard who studies the boundary of life and death, and keeps a retinue on the far side of it.
Copying necromancy spells into your book costs half the time and gold.
Once per turn, killing a creature with a spell of 1st level or higher restores twice the spell's level in hit points, three times for necromancy spells.
You learn animate dead, raise one extra corpse per casting, and your undead gain extra hit points and add your proficiency bonus to weapon damage.
Resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum cannot be reduced.

As an action, an undead you can see within 60 feet makes a Charisma save against your spell save DC (with advantage if its Intelligence is 8 or higher) or becomes friendly and obeys your commands until you use this again. An undead with an Intelligence of 12 or higher that failed repeats the save at the end of every hour, breaking free on a success.
A wizard who changes what things are: matter, shape, and eventually the limits of the body.
Copying transmutation spells into your book costs half the time and gold.
Ten minutes of concentration converts one material into another, such as wood into stone, for an hour.
Craft a stone granting one of darkvision, 10 feet of speed, proficiency in Constitution saves, or resistance to an element, changeable when you cast a transmutation spell.

You add polymorph to your spellbook if it isn't there, and you can cast it without a spell slot, targeting only yourself and becoming a beast of challenge rating 1 or lower; once per short or long rest, though you can still cast it normally with a slot.
Destroy your Transmuter's Stone to transform an object, remove all curses and disease from a creature, restore a creature's youth, or raise the dead.
A battle wizard who blends abjuration and evocation into a fighting style of shields and volleys.
A reaction after being hit or failing a save grants +2 AC or +4 on the save, at the cost of casting only cantrips on your next turn.
Add your Intelligence modifier to initiative.

You can store a number of power surges up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). After a long rest you have one, you gain one whenever you end a spell with dispel magic or counterspell, and you gain one at the end of a short rest if you have none. Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature or object with a wizard spell, you can spend one to deal extra force damage equal to half your wizard level.
While concentrating on a spell, gain +2 AC and +2 on all saving throws.
Arcane Deflection also deals half your wizard level in force damage to up to three creatures within 60 feet.
An elven tradition of sword-dance and spell, trading a heavy spellbook for footwork.
Proficiency with light armor, one one-handed melee weapon, and the Performance skill.
A bonus action for a minute grants +Intelligence to AC, 10 feet of speed, advantage on Acrobatics and a concentration-save bonus; a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest.
Attack twice with the Attack action, and one of those attacks may be a cantrip with a casting time of one action.
A reaction while bladesinging spends a spell slot to reduce damage to you by five times the slot level.
Add your Intelligence modifier (at least +1) to melee weapon damage while bladesinging.
A wizard of Wildemount who manipulates time itself: initiative, durations and dice.

After you or a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, a reaction forces a reroll once you see whether it succeeded, and the second roll stands. Twice per long rest.
Add your Intelligence modifier to initiative.

As an action, a Large or smaller creature you can see within 60 feet makes a Constitution save against your spell save DC or is incapacitated with speed 0 until the end of your next turn or until it takes damage; a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) per long rest.
Store a spell of 4th level or lower in a bead that anyone can break to cast it; recharges on a short or long rest.
A reaction dictates the outcome of a roll within 60 feet as a success or a failure, at the cost of a level of exhaustion.
A wizard of Wildemount who bends weight and gravity, crushing, slowing and hurling.
Halve or double a creature's or object's weight for a minute, changing its speed, carrying capacity and Strength checks.
Any creature you affect with a spell can be moved 5 feet to a space of your choice.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet hits with a weapon attack, a reaction adds 1d10 to its damage; or when a creature within 60 feet takes falling damage, a reaction adds 2d10. A number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) per long rest.

As an action, for a minute (concentration) you emanate a 30-foot field: each hostile creature that starts its turn in it makes a Strength save against your spell save DC, taking 2d10 force damage and having speed 0 until the start of its next turn on a failure, or half damage on a success, after which every foot it moves in the field costs 2 extra feet. Once per long rest, or by expending a spell slot of 3rd level or higher.
A wizard whose spellbook wakes up and starts talking, and whose spells can change their element.
Conjure a magic quill that needs no ink, scribes at speed, and can erase what it wrote.

Your spellbook gains a mind and becomes your spellcasting focus. When you cast a wizard spell with a slot you can change its damage type to one found in another spell in your book of the slot's level; once per long rest you can cast a ritual spell from the book at its normal casting time rather than adding 10 minutes; and over a short rest your quill can turn a blank book into a new home for its mind.

As a bonus action, manifest your spellbook's mind as a Tiny spectral object within 60 feet that sheds dim light in 10 feet, sees in darkness to 60 feet and moves up to 30 feet when you use a bonus action; it ends if it is ever more than 300 feet from you. While it is manifested you can cast a wizard spell from its space a number of times per long rest equal to your proficiency bonus. Manifesting it is free once per long rest, or costs a spell slot of any level.

After a long rest you can create a magic scroll of a 1st- or 2nd-level wizard spell from your book with a casting time of an action; it is cast as if one level higher, and it vanishes once cast or when you finish a long rest.

While your spellbook is on your person you have advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks. If you take damage while the book's mind is manifested, a reaction dismisses it to prevent all of that damage; then roll 3d6, and spells in your book with a combined level at least that total vanish from it until you finish 1d6 long rests (if there aren't enough, you drop to 0 hit points). Once per long rest.
An artificer who works in tinctures and reagents, healing allies and corroding enemies with thrown concoctions.

After a long rest you brew one elixir in an empty flask (two from 6th level, three from 15th), its effect rolled on a d6: healing (2d4 + your Intelligence modifier hit points), swiftness (walking speed 10 feet higher for an hour), resilience (+1 AC for 10 minutes), boldness (a d4 added to attack rolls and saving throws for a minute), flight (a 10-foot flying speed for 10 minutes) or transformation (alter self for 10 minutes). As an action you can expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to brew one more, choosing its effect. An elixir lasts until it is drunk or you finish a long rest.

When you cast a spell with alchemist's supplies as your spellcasting focus, add your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) to one roll of the spell that restores hit points or deals acid, fire, necrotic or poison damage.

A creature that drinks one of your experimental elixirs also gains 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier temporary hit points (minimum 1). With alchemist's supplies as your focus you can cast lesser restoration without a spell slot or preparing it, a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) per long rest.
You gain resistance to acid and poison damage, immunity to the poisoned condition, and can cast greater restoration and heal once per long rest each without a slot.
An artificer who lives inside their own powered armor, built either to guard the line or to strike from the dark.
Proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.
Your armor becomes a magical suit that needs no Strength, cannot be removed against your will, and replaces missing limbs.

Choose Guardian or Infiltrator, and change it on a short or long rest; you use Intelligence for the attack and damage rolls of the armor's weapon. Guardian: thunder gauntlets (a 1d8 thunder melee weapon; a creature hit has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you until the start of your next turn) and Defensive Field (a bonus action gives you temporary hit points equal to your artificer level, a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest). Infiltrator: a lightning launcher (a 1d6 lightning ranged weapon, 90/300 feet, that once on each of your turns deals an extra 1d6 lightning damage to a creature it strikes), Powered Steps (walking speed 5 feet higher) and Dampening Field (advantage on Stealth checks).
Attack twice whenever you take the Attack action.

Your Arcane Armor counts as separate items for your infusions (the armor, the boots, the helmet and the special weapon), and you can infuse two more items at once, provided both are parts of the armor.

Guardian: when a Huge or smaller creature you can see ends its turn within 30 feet of you, a reaction makes it save on Strength against your spell save DC or be pulled up to 25 feet toward you into an unoccupied space, and if it ends within 5 feet of you, you can make a melee weapon attack against it as part of the reaction; a proficiency-bonus number of times per long rest. Infiltrator: a creature your lightning launcher damages glows until the start of your next turn, has disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and the next attack roll against it has advantage and deals an extra 1d6 lightning damage if it hits.
An artificer who builds a small arcane cannon and turns a fight into a siege.

As an action you create a Small or Tiny cannon (AC 18, hit points five times your artificer level) in an unoccupied space within 5 feet that lasts an hour; once per long rest, or by expending a spell slot of 1st level or higher. A bonus action activates it if it is within 60 feet: Flamethrower (a 15-foot cone, 2d8 fire damage, half on a successful Dexterity save), Force Ballista (a ranged spell attack at a creature within 120 feet for 2d8 force damage that pushes it 5 feet) or Protector (it and each creature of your choice within 10 feet of it gain 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier temporary hit points).
A wand, staff or rod becomes your firearm, adding 1d8 to one damage roll of each artificer spell you cast through it.
Your cannon deals an extra 1d8, and you can detonate it as an action for 3d8 force damage in a 20-foot radius, halved on a successful Dexterity save.
You can have two cannons at once, and you and your allies have half cover within 10 feet of one.
An artificer who fights beside a construct companion and repairs the party as readily as their gear.
Proficiency with martial weapons, and you use Intelligence instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage with magic weapons.

You build a steel defender that fights beside you and acts on your initiative right after you, taking the Dodge action unless you spend a bonus action to command it. It has AC 15 and 2 + your Intelligence modifier + five times your artificer level hit points, attacks with Force-Empowered Rend (a melee attack using your spell attack modifier for 1d8 + your proficiency bonus force damage), and its Deflect Attack reaction gives disadvantage to one attack against a creature other than itself within 5 feet of it.
Attack twice whenever you take the Attack action.

When your magic weapon or your steel defender hits a target, once per turn you can deal it an extra 2d6 force damage or restore 2d6 hit points to a creature or object you can see within 30 feet of it, a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) per long rest.
Arcane Jolt rises to 4d6, your defender gains +2 AC, and its deflecting reaction also deals force damage to the attacker.
